newsitem.title: CHINA: China copper group in Yunnan to boost output.
newsitem.headline: China copper group in Yunnan to boost output.

text.p: A new production group in China's southwestern province of Yunnan plans to boost its output of copper ore and products over the next five years, company officials said on Friday.
The Yunnan Copper Industry (Group) Co started business on August 19 after a merger of provincial mines and a smelter.
The new group would boost output of electrolytic copper to 150,000 tonnes a year by 2000 from the current 90,000 tonnes, general manager Zhou Paixiang told Reuters.
The group's mines would boost their annual output of copper ore to 60,000 tonnes from 45,000 tonnes, he said.
To cover a shortfall between the group's mine output and the demand from its smelters, copper imports of 50,000 tonnes a year or more would be needed by the end of the century, he said.
The output of other minerals would also be raised through higher productivity and increased investment, Zhou said.
The production of gold would rise to about five tonnes a year by 2000 from three tonnes currently.
